task.piece: MySQL's Tables (t02): every option the MySQL engine declares (engines/mysql/src/options.rs) written as rows of MySQL's own tables (engines/mysql/schema) and read back, so every MySQL sample goes through the cortex's rows and MySQL's and comes back the same. And the kit made to require Tables of an engine that reads. Nothing else: no option added, renamed or removed, no table of engines/mysql/schema changed, no SQLite (t05).

module.public: nothing: Mysql's impl of Tables, reached by Engine::tables
module.step: files() is every table file of engines/mysql/schema, embedded with include_str!, by its name, in name order; integrity() is engines/mysql/schema/integrity.sql; migrations() is empty.

An option's value goes to its column as the layout's JSON holds it: a flag as the integer 1 or 0, an integer as an integer, text and a word of one of as text, exactly as written; a column with no option is null. A flag whose column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (linear and "columns" of mysql__partitioning_options, linear of mysql__subpartitionings, aggregate of mysql__loadable_functions, "desc" of mysql__key_column_options) is an option MySQL's reader writes only when true (engines/mysql/src/read/table.rs, read/program.rs, read/mod.rs): 1 is the option true, 0 the option absent, and read() sets it only on 1. A row is written only when at least one of its columns is not null, or a child row (steps 4 and 6) needs it as its parent; read() sets an option only for a column that is not null, so a row of nulls sets nothing.

A namespace's options charset, collation, encryption and read_only go to mysql__database_options by their names. A table's options go to mysql__table_options, each to the column of its name (connection to "connection"), but union and outside_references: union, the list of the tables a MERGE table joins, is one row of mysql__merge_tables per entry, in order, its text in table_name (its parent row in mysql__table_options written for it); outside_references, the list of the foreign keys kept as written, one row of mysql__outside_references per entry, in order, its text in text.

A view's algorithm, check_option and security go to mysql__view_options; its column_list, one row of mysql__view_column_names per name, in order (its parent row written for it). definer, sql_mode, character_set_client, collation_connection, time_zone, follows, precedes and disabled_on_replica, on a view, procedure, function, trigger, event or library, go to mysql__program_context. A routine's data_access goes to mysql__routine_options and its imports, one row of mysql__routine_imports per library, in order. A loadable function's soname, aggregate and returns go to mysql__loadable_functions; a tablespace's datafile, file_block_size, engine, autoextend_size, encryption and engine_attribute to mysql__tablespaces; a spatial reference system's srid, definition, organization and organization_srid to mysql__spatial_reference_systems.

A column's options go to mysql__column_options by their names ("binary" quoted). A key's method, comment, key_block_size, invisible and engine_attribute go to mysql__key_options; its parts, one shape per column in order, each of length and desc, go to mysql__key_column_options, one row for each column whose shape holds either, its id the key column's id (t02 step 2), length its length or null, "desc" 1 when desc is true else 0; read() rebuilds parts with one shape per column of the key, JSON null for a column without a row (as MySQL's reader writes it), when the key has at least one row, and sets no parts otherwise. A key holds column parts only: MySQL's reader makes a unique key with an expression part an index, and a primary key holds no expression (engines/mysql/src/read/table.rs, its unique key), so parts and the key's columns are one for one. An index's comment, key_block_size, parser, invisible and engine_attribute go to mysql__index_options; an index part's length to mysql__index_part_options. A check's not_enforced to mysql__check_options. A link's inline to mysql__link_options.

A partitioning's linear, algorithm, count and columns go to mysql__partitioning_options; its subpartition, an object of strategy, by, linear and count, to mysql__subpartitionings, by in by_text and linear 0 when absent. A partition's engine, comment, data_directory, index_directory, max_rows, min_rows and tablespace go to mysql__partition_options, its id the partition's; its subpartitions, each an object of name and those same options, are one row of mysql__subpartitions per entry, in order, id `<partition>.sub<n>`, and that subpartition's options a row of mysql__partition_options with its id.
An option of any part that steps 3 to 6 do not place is the error of t02 step 5, naming the part and the option; none of the options of options.rs is such an option.
An engine that reads (Engine::read is Some) and has no Tables is the kit's finding `it reads schemas, but has no tables to keep them in`.

tests.how: Rust tests on schemas the MySQL engine reads from SQL text of each test's own, and on the samples under engines/mysql/tests; the rows are inspected as Rows; no test reaches a database or the network.
tests.prove: files() holds every file of engines/mysql/schema but integrity.sql, by its name, and integrity() is its integrity.sql
a flag is written as 1 or 0, a value exactly as written, and a row of nulls is never written nor sets an option
a flag whose column is not null with default 0 comes back only when it was true, and is absent when it was absent
a table's options, its merge tables and its outside references are rows of their tables, in order, and come back the same

a view's options and column names, a program's context, a routine's data access and imports, a loadable function, a tablespace and a spatial reference system are rows of their tables and come back the same
a key's parts are rows only for the columns with a length or desc, and come back as one shape per column, null for a column without either
column, index, index part, check and link options are rows of their tables and come back the same
a subpartitioned table's partitions and subpartitions, with their options, are rows of their tables and come back the same
an option no step places is the error naming the part and the option
the MySQL engine passes the conformance kit on every sample, its tables' round trip included, and the kit finds an engine that reads with no tables
